== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L13
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L86-L172
    86  const USAGE: &str = "\
    87  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>]
    88                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    89                 [--] FILE.ndjson
    90         con-ron --help
    91  
    92    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    93    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    94    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    95    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    96    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    97    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    98    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
    99    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   100    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   101  
   102    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   103                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   104                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   105                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  The
   106                      same two statements are PROVED about this program's
   107                      pipeline (ConRon.Capstone.model_exists and
   108                      no_False_declaration, on the Aeneas model of the Rust),
   109                      using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and
   110                      Quot.sound.  What they still assume are hypotheses, not
   111                      axioms: that the driver runs the extracted stages in the
   112                      order it does on the file's bytes.  They hold at every pin
   113                      text and every prelude.  OVERVIEW.md section 3.1 lists
   114                      them.
   115    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   116                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   117                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   118    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   119                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   120                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   121                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   122                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   123                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   124                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   125                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   126                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   127                      error, as in con-leche.
   128    --                every argument after it is a file, whatever it is called;
   129                      FILE.ndjson is a regular file, read forward (a FIFO or a
   130                      directory is exit 3)
   131  
   132  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   133  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   134  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   135  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   136  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   137  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   138  
   139  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   140  exits 3 without reading its input.
   141  
   142  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   143  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   144  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   145  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   146  
   147  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   148  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   149  built-in prelude's own records are not counted; a stream record that declares
   150  a prelude declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the
   151  number of environment CONSTANTS is not.
   152  
   153  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   154  checker's own little prelude -- the five pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, Empty,
   155  False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   156  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   157  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   158  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   159  hash-consed together.
   160  
   161  NO PREPROCESSOR, NO MODELS.  The input is a RAW lean4export stream: there is no
   162  external tool, no dependency and no spawn.  Every inductive block --
   163  structures, sums, indexed families, recursive, reflexive, mutual and nested
   164  blocks -- is installed by the ONE uniform installer: it checks the type formers
   165  and constructors, runs the positivity check, and GENERATES the block's
   166  recursors; the stream's recursor records are compared with the generated ones
   167  up to definitional equality, types and rules, and what is installed is the
   168  stream's type and rules' right-hand sides.  No model is ever read from the input: a
   169  stream record whose name carries a `_model` component is an ordinary
   170  declaration with no effect on any block.  A block whose shape the installer
   171  does not recognise declines (exit 2), naming it.  The binary reads no
   172  environment variable.";

    19  //! |---|---|---|

    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L16-L135
    16  /-!
    17  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    18  
    19  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    20  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    21  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    22  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    23  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    24  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    25  
    26  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    27    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    28  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    29    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    30  
    31  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    32  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    33  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    34  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    35  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    36  
    37  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    38  
    39  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    40  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    41  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    42  
    43      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    44        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    45  
    46  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    47  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    48  of `check_main`.
    49  
    50  and the twin runs the same six stages (`Arena/Main.lean`'s
    51  `runPipelineHead`/`runPipelineTail` drive them for `con-ron-lean`).  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    52  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    53  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    54  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    55  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `h7` the freeze, `h8`
    56  phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    57  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is
    58  the contract of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's
    59  two verified closures, written out (task #98-H8): index lists `ws`, one per
    60  worker, covering every pending record, and for each a `foldlM` of
    61  `check_pending` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That
    62  contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    63  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.  `parallelAll_of_pool` reads it as
    64  `Phased.lean`'s `ParallelAll`, and `PoolAccepts.toParts` turns that into one
    65  accepting fold per worker over the records it checked.
    66  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    67  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    68  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    69  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    70  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    71  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    72  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    73  
    74  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    75     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    76     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    77     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    78  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    79     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    80     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    81     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    82     (`stages_no_False`, through the pure fold);
    83  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    84     model.
    85  
    86  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    87  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    88  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    89  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    90  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    91  
    92  ## The named hypotheses
    93  
    94  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    95  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    96  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    97  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    98  `prepare_prelude`).  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    99  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
   100  they assume is exactly:
   101  
   102  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   103    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   104    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   105    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   106    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   107    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam — the one seam left.
   108  
   109  Former hypotheses, now theorems or gone (DESIGN.md's task #97-COMPOSE and
   110  #98-HEADLINE sections tag each with its owning lane):
   111  
   112  * ~~`InitRel`~~ — the Rust start state is related to the twin's: a theorem
   113    since task #97-P5-Top (`Refine2/Checker/Init.lean`'s `init_rel`);
   114  * ~~`hk : CoreSpec .verified Arena.checkFuel`~~ — Theorem 1's Core tier
   115    spec: a theorem since task #97-P3-Core round 6
   116    (`Bridge/Checker/Hyp.lean`'s `CoreSpec.of_core`);
   117  * ~~`hind : IndSpec .verified`~~ — Theorem 1's inductive tier spec:
   118    `Bridge/Inductives/Decl.lean`'s `indSpec_of_bridge` since task #97-P3-Ind
   119    round 8 (the stage lemmas below still take it as a parameter);
   120  * ~~`hbytes`~~ — the prelude's bytes are con-leche's: not needed since task
   121    #98-HEADLINE.  con-leche's `preparePrelude` puts the prelude's records into
   122    the checked stream, so soundness holds whatever the prelude parses to
   123    (`Bridge/Frontend/Prepare.lean`'s `builtinPreludeE_run` is parametric in
   124    the bytes).  The gate `scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check` stays, as the
   125    claim that con-ron ships con-leche's prelude;
   126  * ~~`hsc : ScanSpec`~~ — Theorem 2's scanner seam: a theorem since task
   127    #97-P5-Front (`Refine2/Frontend/Scan/Spec.lean`'s `scanSpec`);
   128  * ~~`hpers`, `hest`, `hst0`~~ — the start state and tier were universally
   129    quantified with three equations; since task #98-HEADLINE they are the

    35      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L30
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```
    14  //!
    15  //! (tier 0 = persistent, 1 = scratch; the index is into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S
    16  //! array of THAT TIER).  The zero word is a narrow handle — tag 0,
    17  //! persistent, slot 0 — which is the twin's `default : Idx k` and every
    18  //! `of_word(0)` below: the anonymous name, the level `zero`, a handle that
    19  //! decodes.  An expression `app` array holds 2^30 = 1 073 741 824 nodes per
    20  //! tier and every other constructor array 2^26 =
    21  //! 67 108 864: apps are 85 % of an export's expression nodes, so they are the
    22  //! array that runs out first, and they get the room.  Only the expression
    23  //! `app` tag is wide — a level `param` handle is narrow although `LTAG_PARAM`
    24  //! has `ETAG_APP`'s value — and `word_tag` reads `ETAG_APP` off a word with
    25  //! bit 30 set, so the tag of a handle is read the same way for all four
    26  //! kinds.
    27  //!
    28  //! The tier is the TOP bit, above both shapes' index, so a persistent
    29  //! handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes and goes
    30  //! (con-leche's lesson 6).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3624-L3659
  3624  
  3625      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:482-502 EStore.intern
  3626      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3627      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3628      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3629      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3630      ///
  3631      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3632      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3633      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3634      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3635      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3636      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3637      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3638      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3639      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3640      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3641      ///
  3642      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3643      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3644      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3645      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3646          match v {
  3647              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3648              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3649              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3650              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3651              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3652              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3653              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3654              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3655              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3656              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3657          }
  3658      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3909-L3956
  3909      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3910          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  3911          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  3912              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  3913                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  3914              } else {
  3915                  true
  3916              }
  3917          } else {
  3918              false
  3919          };
  3920          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  3921              None
  3922          } else if pers.frozen {
  3923              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  3924          } else {
  3925              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  3926          };
  3927          match hit {
  3928              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  3929              None => {
  3930                  if self.scratch_on {
  3931                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  3932                      match at.1 {
  3933                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  3934                          None => {
  3935                              if self.scr.apps.full_wide() {
  3936                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3937                              } else {
  3938                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3939                                  let h: EIdx =
  3940                                      EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  3941                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  3942                                  Ok(h)
  3943                              }
  3944                          }
  3945                      }
  3946                  } else if self.pers.apps.full_wide() {
  3947                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3948                  } else {
  3949                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3950                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  3951                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  3952                      Ok(h)
  3953                  }
  3954              }
  3955          }
  3956      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core.rs#L10424-L10464
 10424  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:336-343 CState.flushed
 10425  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3693-3699 flushCaches` — **what
 10426  /// the per-declaration bracket does to the caches**: it drops them whole,
 10427  /// which is con-leche's own `flushC`, the operation its driver runs at exactly
 10428  /// this point.
 10429  ///
 10430  /// Task #97-P4c ported DESIGN.md §8.3's survivor policy instead — keep the
 10431  /// rows whose key AND value are persistent — which is sound and strictly more
 10432  /// caching; task #97f measured what it costs (`filter` is `O(table)` and the
 10433  /// survivors accumulate, so the fold pays `O(declarations × surviving rows)`:
 10434  /// 16 % of `Init`'s first 4 380 declarations' cycles, 213 s → 124 s).  The
 10435  /// twin's `Caches.dropScratchEntries` stays as the SPECIFICATION of a
 10436  /// surviving row, and so does `Caches::drop_scratch_entries` below it with
 10437  /// its eleven journals — P3 needs it to state that flushing is sound.
 10438  pub fn flush_caches(st: &mut AState) {
 10439      st.caches.reset();
 10440  }
 10441  
 10442  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10443  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3701-3709 dropScratch` — drop the
 10444  /// scratch tier of the store and the cache entries that name it, in one
 10445  /// operation, so the two halves cannot drift apart; and **thaw** the store:
 10446  /// the tier `enter_scratch` handed out comes back (task #98-FREEZE), so the
 10447  /// store is owned and scratch-off again.
 10448  pub fn drop_scratch(st: &mut AState, tier: PersTier) {
 10449      flush_caches(st);
 10450      st.store.thaw(tier);
 10451  }
 10452  
 10453  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, opened** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10454  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3711-3718 enterScratch` — turn the
 10455  /// scratch tier on, and clear the per-call memo tables of `Memos`, which
 10456  /// belong to no tier and whose keys the new tier may reuse.  **Opening a
 10457  /// bracket is freezing the store** (task #98-FREEZE): its persistent tables
 10458  /// are handed back as the `PersTier` every read inside the bracket goes
 10459  /// through and promotion writes, and every append inside it is a scratch
 10460  /// append.
 10461  pub fn enter_scratch(st: &mut AState) -> PersTier {
 10462      st.memos.reset();
 10463      st.store.freeze()
 10464  }

     1  //! `arena::promote` — the scratch → persistent copy (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-2).
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Promote.lean`, declaration for
     4  //! declaration, under DESIGN.md §8.6's lockstep ruling.
     5  //!
     6  //! DESIGN.md §8.3, "**Phase A runs in the scratch tier too, with promotion**":
     7  //!
     8  //! > The install phase (annotate the type and the value, infer, defeq) was
     9  //! > interning every intermediate into the persistent tier — on `Init` 5.06 M
    10  //! > permanent nodes on top of the parse's 6.14 M (+82 %) […].  The arena's
    11  //! > answer is con-leche #64's: phase A opens the scratch tier like phase B,
    12  //! > and the two handles it must keep (the annotated type, the annotated
    13  //! > value) are **promoted** — a memoised structural copy scratch →
    14  //! > persistent […] before the tier is dropped.  Persistent handles are
    15  //! > promoted to themselves.
    16  //!
    17  //! This module is that copy, at all four handle kinds and lifted to
    18  //! `arena::env`'s declaration layer, plus `promote_new` — the entry
    19  //! `arena::checker`'s two fold steps call, which promotes a step's NEWLY
    20  //! INSTALLED constants in place.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## What it is
    23  //!
    24  //! `view` the node, promote its children, `intern` the result into the
    25  //! PERSISTENT tier (`arena::store`'s `intern_persistent` family, whose section
    26  //! note carries the WF obligations).  Three properties make it cheap and make
    27  //! it right:
    28  //!
    29  //! * **a persistent handle promotes to itself**, by one tier-bit test
    30  //!   (`is_persistent`) and no store access at all.  Most of what a step
    31  //!   leaves behind IS the parsed term (since task #119 a value kind's record
    32  //!   is exactly the parsed one), so the walk stops at the first persistent
    33  //!   node on every branch;
    34  //! * **the memo makes it `O(result)`** and not `O(unfolding)`: the subject is
    35  //!   a hash-consed DAG, and an unmemoised structural copy of a DAG is the
    36  //!   mistake task #97g's item 5 found three times over.  The memo is per
    37  //!   DECLARATION — a scratch handle means nothing once the tier is dropped —
    38  //!   and it is threaded as an argument-and-result pair, a moved
    39  //!   `ron::HashMap` returned, which is `frontend::proj_rec`'s spelling for its
    40  //!   `seen` set and `arena::expr_ops`' for the three memoized scope walks;

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L616-L638
   616  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
   617  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its phase-B worker reads the
   618  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Phased.lean`).
   619  /// **The persistent tier out of the store and into a value** (task
   620  /// #97-P6-6b's driver function, moved here by task #97-P5-Driver): the four
   621  /// persistent tables move into one `PersTier` handed back `frozen`, for the
   622  /// phase-B workers to read.  Task #98-FREEZE: this is a pure MOVE — the
   623  /// store's scratch tiers and flags are untouched (a worker's store is its own,
   624  /// `worker_state`), there is no flag to test and so no decline (`M_REFREEZE`
   625  /// is gone), and `thaw_tier` puts the tables back where they were.  The
   626  /// driver's store is not read between the two.
   627  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore) -> PersTier {
   628      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
   629      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
   630      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
   631      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
   632      PersTier {
   633          frozen: true,
   634          n,
   635          l,
   636          ls,
   637          e,
   638      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L466-L513
   466  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   467  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   468  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   469  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:386-388 Expr.allLevelParamsDefinedFast
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/DeclCheck.lean:190-192 Expr.constsResolveFFast
   473  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   474  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   475  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   476  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   477  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   478  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   479  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   480  ///
   481  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   482  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   483  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   484  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   485  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   486  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   487  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   488  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   489  ///
   490  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   491  /// |---|---:|
   492  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   493  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   494  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   495  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   496  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   497  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   498  ///
   499  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   500  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   501  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   502  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   503  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   504  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   505      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   506      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   507          HashMap::new()
   508      } else {
   509          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   510          reset_map(&mut m2);
   511          m2
   512      }
   513  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L326-L513
   326      let mode_tag = if a.verified {
   327          "--verified"
   328      } else {

   330      };

   333      } else {
   334          CheckMode::Trusted
   335      };

   337      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   338      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`
   339      let mut st = AState::empty();
   340      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a phase-B worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task
   341      // #97-P6-6b).  The parse and phase A's setup own their own — the store
   342      // is owned (not frozen) outside a declaration bracket — so what they are
   343      // handed here is the EMPTY tier, and the single-lane computation is

   346      // `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every worker; `check_decls_driver` is
   347      // where that happens.
   348      // ConRon.Capstone: `emptyTier`
   349      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   350      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   351      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   352      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   353      // every `drop_scratch` of the run.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   354      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   355      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   356      // unlikely.
   357      // ConRon.Capstone: h1
   358      match con_ron_core::arena::pins::intern_reserved_pins(pers, &mut st) {
   359          Ok(()) => (),
   360          Err(e) => {
   361              eprintln!(
   362                  "con-ron: the reserved-name pins do not intern ({}) ({})",
   363                  con_ron::driver::message(&e),
   364                  mode_tag
   365              );
   366              return 3;
   367          }
   368      }
   369      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   370      // ConRon.Capstone: h2
   371      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &mut st) {
   372          Ok(p) => p,
   373          Err((e, line)) => {
   374              let what = match classify(&e) {
   375                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   376                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   377                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   378              };
   379              eprintln!(
   380                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   381                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   382                  what, mode_tag
   383              );
   384              return 3;
   385          }
   386      };
   387      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   388      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   389      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   390      // store above.  No model is ever read from the input: every inductive
   391      // block — mutual and nested included — installs through the kernel's
   392      // uniform installer, unconditionally (task #105).
   393      // ConRon.Capstone: hreads, h3 (`parse_source` over the file's handle)
   394      let parsed: ParseResultD = match driver::parse_export_stream_d(
   395          pers,
   396          &mut st,
   397          file,
   398          export_c::CHUNK_SIZE,
   399      ) {
   400          Err(e) => {
   401              eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", con_ron::render::display_path(file), e);
   402              return 3;
   403          }
   404          Ok((Err((e, line)), _)) => match classify(&e) {
   405              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   406                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   407                  return 2;
   408              }
   409              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   410              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   411              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   412                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   413                  return 1;
   414              }
   415              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   416                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", con_ron::render::display_path(file), line, msg);
   417                  return 3;
   418              }
   419          },
   420          Ok((Ok(r), _)) => r,
   421      };
   422      let file_records = parsed.decls.len();
   423      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   424      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   425      // produced indexes into it.
   426      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   427      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   428      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   429      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   430      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   431      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   432      // ConRon.Capstone: h4
   433      let prepared = match prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed.decls) {
   434          Ok(p) => p,
   435          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   436      };
   437      // the ground hoist's receipt
   438      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   439          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   440              .hoisted
   441              .iter()
   442              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   443              .collect();
   444          eprintln!(
   445              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   446               they ground: {}",
   447              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   448              names.join(", ")
   449          );
   450      }
   451      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   452      // outside the theorems)
   453      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {
   454          Ok(p) => p,
   455          Err(e) => {
   456              eprintln!("con-ron: {}", e);
   457              return 3;
   458          }
   459      };
   460      // The heartbeat's first line: the parse and the preparation are done.
   461      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(a.progress, t0);
   462      hb.parse_done(
   463          prepared.decls.len(),
   464          file_records,
   465          prepared.synthesised,
   466          (
   467              st.store.node_count(pers),
   468              st.store.ls().node_count(pers),
   469              st.store.ns().node_count(pers),
   470          ),
   471      );
   472      // **THE STARTUP PIN WALK** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d): every
   473      // pinned datum the checker compares a stream record against — the six
   474      // basis blocks in both forms, the axiom pins, the reserved names and the
   475      // `Nat`-operation variants — interned ONCE, here, while the scratch tier
   476      // is still off, so that nothing the fold compares against lives in a tier
   477      // that is about to vanish.  Its result is the fold's pin parameter.
   478      // ConRon.Capstone: h5
   479      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(pers, &mut st, &pins) {
   480          Ok(p) => p,
   481          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   482      };
   483      // ONE driver, and the heartbeat is printed between its steps
   484      // (`driver::check_decls_driver`: phase A, the frozen tier, and the pool
   485      // for its phase B).
   486      let jobs: u64 = match a.jobs {
   487          Some(n) => n,
   488          None => con_ron::driver::default_jobs(),
   489      };
   490      // ONE lane, whatever the flags: the driver is what freezes the persistent
   491      // tier at the phase boundary and phase B is the pool at every worker count
   492      // (task #97-P6-6b), so a run with no heartbeat is the same computation as
   493      // a run with one and `install_then_check` is no longer a second path.
   494      // ConRon.Capstone: h6, h7, h8 (the driver's three steps, either observer)
   495      let verdict = if a.progress > 0 {
   496          driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, &prepared.decls, jobs, &mut hb)
   497      } else {
   498          let mut silent = driver::Silent;
   499          driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, &prepared.decls, jobs, &mut silent)
   500      };
   501      // **The headline number is the FILE's declaration-record count**: the
   502      // records the PARSE produced, which are the file's own.  Nothing the
   503      // preparation does moves it.
   504      let stream_records = file_records as u64;
   505      let code = match &verdict {
   506          Ok(_) => driver::verdict_accept(stream_records, mode_tag),
   507          Err((e, i)) => {
   508              driver::verdict_failure(pers, &st.store, &prepared.decls, e, *i, mode_tag, t0)
   509          }
   510      };
   511      exit_after_verdict(code)
   512  }
   513  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty-one names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is.
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L915-L956
   915  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:170-178 foldChunks
   916  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   917  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   918  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   919  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   920  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   921  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   922  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   923      /// The open reader.
   924      pub h: &'a mut R,
   925      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   926      pub chunk: usize,
   927      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   928      pub chunks: u64,
   929      /// The first read failure, if any.
   930      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   931  }
   932  
   933  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:170-178 foldChunks
   934  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   935      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:170-178 foldChunks
   936      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   937      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   938          if self.err.is_some() {
   939              return Vec::new();
   940          }
   941          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   942          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   943              Ok(n) => {
   944                  buf.truncate(n);
   945                  if n > 0 {
   946                      self.chunks += 1;
   947                  }
   948                  buf
   949              }
   950              Err(e) => {
   951                  self.err = Some(e);
   952                  Vec::new()
   953              }
   954          }
   955      }
   956  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1-L41
     1  //! `arena::checker` — the declaration fold, over handles.
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean`, which is con-leche's
     4  //! `Kernel/Checker.lean`'s `checkDecl`/`checkDeclsPure` and
     5  //! `Cached/Installed.lean`'s two-phase `checkDecls`.
     6  //!
     7  //! ## Two folds, and which is which
     8  //!
     9  //! * **`check_decls_pure`** is the THEOREM's shape —
    10  //!   `ConLeche/Model/Fold.lean`'s `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` consumes it, and
    11  //!   DESIGN.md §8.2's Theorem 1 folds `checkDecl` over the stream.  One step
    12  //!   per record, install and check together.
    13  //! * **`install_then_check`** is what the BINARY runs: phase A installs every
    14  //!   record, guarding its header and its value but not inferring; phase B
    15  //!   checks each recorded declaration against the PREFIX VIEW it was installed
    16  //!   at.  con-leche proves the two are the same accept
    17  //!   (`fullyChecked_checkDecls`); the arena's two call the same `checkDecl`
    18  //!   pieces, which is what keeps them the same computation.
    19  //!
    20  //! ## Every step is bracketed
    21  //!
    22  //! DESIGN.md §8.3: "Persistent = parse + installed environment; scratch = one
    23  //! declaration's check."  Both phases and both folds run each record inside
    24  //! `enter_scratch` … `drop_scratch`.  Phase B's `check_pending` brackets
    25  //! `check_value_group`, and every node it appends goes with the tier.  Phase
    26  //! A's `install_step` brackets the install too (the fallback
    27  //! `install_step_other` included), because the ordinary step's installers
    28  //! infer and inference interns: `promote` copies exactly what leaves the step
    29  //! — the installed constants and the pending record — to the persistent tier
    30  //! before the drop (see `install_step`).
    31  //! `check_decls_pure`'s step, `check_decl_step`, is bracketed the same way.
    32  //!
    33  //! ## The pins are interned at startup
    34  //!
    35  //! `intern_all_pins` is DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d's one-time tree walk, and it is what
    36  //! makes every later `pin`/`intern_ci` of the same datum return the PERSISTENT
    37  //! handle whatever tier is live (§8.3: `intern` probes the persistent table
    38  //! first).  Without it a reserved name first interned inside a scratch tier
    39  //! would compare unequal to the stream's own persistent copy of it, which is
    40  //! the one way hash-consing can go wrong across the tier boundary.
    41  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L184-L240
   184  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:139-177 installStepC
   185  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:157-214 installStep` — **phase
   186  /// A's step, bracketed**; `i` is the fold position the record is tagged with.
   187  ///
   188  /// **The bracket** (DESIGN.md §8.3, "Phase A runs in the scratch tier too,
   189  /// with promotion", task #97-P6-2):
   190  ///
   191  /// ```text
   192  /// flush_caches; enter_scratch; <the step>; promote; drop_scratch
   193  /// ```
   194  ///
   195  /// `promote` (`arena::promote`) is the memoised structural copy scratch →
   196  /// persistent, run on **exactly what leaves the step**: the `k` constants and
   197  /// the `kt` projection tables the step installed (`promote_new`) and the
   198  /// pending record (`promote_vg`, at the
   199  /// SAME memo).  A persistent handle promotes to itself, so a record that
   200  /// installs what the parse already built — every value kind since task #119,
   201  /// whose install half interns nothing — pays one tier-bit test per handle;
   202  /// the blocks the ordinary step installs (inductives, the basis) still build
   203  /// terms.  The flush stays where con-leche puts it, at the head
   204  /// (`installGuardsC` and the `.thmDecl` arm's own `flushC`, and
   205  /// `checkDeclStepC`'s), so every phase-A record starts with EMPTY caches.
   206  pub fn install_step(
   207      _pers: &PersTier,
   208      st: &mut AState,
   209      mode: &CheckMode,
   210      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   211      i: u64,
   212      fe: IFEnv,
   213      pend: Vec<PendingCheck>,
   214      pd: &IDeclaration,
   215  ) -> Result<(IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>), CheckError> {
   216      let vis: u64 = fe.visible_below;
   217      let nt: u64 = fe.env.tables.len() as u64;
   218      flush_caches(st);
   219      let mut tier: PersTier = enter_scratch(st);
   220      match install_step_go(&tier, st, mode, pins, fe, pd) {
   221          Err(e) => {
   222              drop_scratch(st, tier);
   223              Err(e)
   224          }
   225          Ok((fe2, vg_opt)) => {
   226              let k: u64 = fe2.visible_below - vis;
   227              let kt: u64 = fe2.env.tables.len() as u64 - nt;
   228              match vg_opt {
   229                  None => match promote_new(&mut tier, st, PMemo::empty(), CORE_WALK_FUEL, k, kt, fe2) {
   230                      Err(e) => {
   231                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   232                          Err(e)
   233                      }
   234                      Ok((_, fe3)) => {
   235                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   236                          Ok((fe3, pend))
   237                      }
   238                  },
   239                  Some(vg) => install_step_promote(tier, st, i, vis, k, kt, fe2, pend, vg),
   240              }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L507-L600
   507  
   508  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:317-334 checkDecls
   509  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:50-210 checkDeclsIO
   510  /// **The driver**: the two-phase fold with the boundary visible — a straight
   511  /// line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the pool for
   512  /// phase B (tasks #97-P5-Driver, #98-POOL).  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   513  ///
   514  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   515  /// |---|---|---|
   516  /// | phase A | `checker::install_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   517  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call's value |
   518  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..pend.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `check_pending tier st mode fe pend[k]` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   519  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   520  ///
   521  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   522  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   523  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every record was checked by some worker,
   524  /// each worker folding `check_pending` over the records it claimed on ONE
   525  /// `worker_state`.  Everything else here is the observer, which only ever
   526  /// holds `&` the state (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the
   527  /// other lines through `&st.store` and the worker's `&AState`), so it cannot
   528  /// change an outcome.
   529  ///
   530  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN** (task #97-P6-6b).  Phase A
   531  /// owns its persistent tier and appends to it; at the boundary
   532  /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves the four stores' persistent tables out into
   533  /// one `PersTier`, handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those
   534  /// tables, and a worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so
   535  /// every append there is a scratch append (task #98-FREEZE).  The
   536  /// installed index goes to the workers by reference, since `check_pending`
   537  /// takes the visibility bound as a scalar — so `n` workers share one
   538  /// environment and one term DAG and own nothing but a scratch tier, their
   539  /// caches and a copy of the pin handles (`checker::worker_state`).
   540  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   541      pers: &PersTier,
   542      st: &mut AState,
   543      mode: &CheckMode,
   544      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   545      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   546      jobs: u64,
   547      obs: &mut O,
   548  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   549      let total = ds.len();
   550      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   551      let p = match checker::install_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   552          Err(e) => {
   553              obs.install_failed(e.1, total);
   554              return Err(e);
   555          }
   556          Ok(p) => p,
   557      };
   558      let (_n_installed, fe, pend): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>) = p;
   559      let m = pend.len();
   560      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m);
   561      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   562      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   563      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier leaves the state and becomes a
   564      // value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   565      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   566      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   567      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store);
   568      // PHASE B: `check_pending` at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   569      // folding it over the records it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the
   570      // verdict and the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at
   571      // every `--jobs` (the least failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   572      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   573      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   574      let r = parallel_all(
   575          m,
   576          workers,
   577          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   578          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]),
   579          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, w, m, &pend[k]),
   580      );
   581      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   582          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   583          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   584      };
   585      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   586      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   587      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   588      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   589      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   590      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   591      checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   592      match phase_b_verdict(&pend, r) {
   593          Err((e, pos)) => {
   594              obs.check_failed(pos);
   595              Err((e, pos))
   596          }
   597          Ok(()) => {
   598              obs.check_done(m);
   599              Ok(fe)
   600          }

    30  //! ## What a worker is, in phase B
    31  //!
    32  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what phase B is: "the persistent tier is immutable
    33  //! in phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**",
    34  //! and task #97-P6-6 verified it in the code (`check_pending` is the bracket;
    35  //! the persistent interns' only caller is phase A's `arena::promote`, which

    40  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier` and
    41  //! the installed `&IFEnv` (by reference: `check_pending` takes the record's
    42  //! prefix bound as a scalar, `pc.vis`, so a worker costs no environment copy

   670  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:213-227 checkWorker
   671  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:33-40 AState.worker` — the twin's
   672  /// phase-B worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
   673  /// **A phase-B worker's start state** (task #97-P6-6b's `pool::worker_state`,

   227  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:236-269 checkPool
   228  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   229  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   230  ///
   231  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by exactly one
   232  /// > worker, each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step`
   233  /// > over its claimed indices in claim order (increasing), and every step
   234  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   235  ///
   236  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   237  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   238  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   239  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   240  ///
   241  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   242  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   243  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   244  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   245  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   246  /// not depend on it.
   247  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   248      n: usize,
   249      workers: usize,
   250      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   251      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   252      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   253  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L185-L208
   185  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   186  readback of an expression handle. -/
   187  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   188    | 0, _ => none
   189    | f + 1, i =>
   190      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   191        match v with
   192        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   193        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   194        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   195        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   196        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   197        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   198        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .letE ty w b =>
   200          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   201        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   202        | .proj n k e =>
   203          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   204  
   205  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the readback of an
   206  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   207  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   208    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds its handle shape's index range (2^30 for `app`, 2^26 for the rest), so the index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation or predicate** (`Rel.lean`'s `RelE`
    26     family, `Grind.lean`'s `Ans`/`MapRel`), never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`): every failure site goes
    30     through it, so one spec covers them all and the Rust has one function to
    31     match.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L60-L76
    60  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    61  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    62  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    63  
    64  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    65  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    66  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    67  
    68  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    69  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    70  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    71  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    72  inversion). -/
    73  @[expose] def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
    74      Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    76      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Rel.lean#L59-L76
    59  /-! ## The core grade -/
    60  
    61  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step
    62  preserves the whole checking invariant, by `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s
    63  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one
    64  and keep its own hypothesis. -/
    65  theorem PStep.toCore {μ : CheckMode} {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} {s s' : AState}
    66      (h : PStep s s') (hc : CheckOK μ false env fe s) : CoreStep μ env fe s s' :=
    67    ⟨hc.monoF h.ok h.ext h.cframe h.pins, h.ext, h.pins⟩
    68  
    69  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/Cached/SimC.lean:366 SimC — **the CORE grade's
    70  statement**: the same at a function that calls the knot, so the invariant is
    71  `CheckOK` and the frame is `CoreStep`.  The pure side's fuel existential lives
    72  inside `R`, as `Bridge/Core/Knot.lean`'s `SimE` has it. -/
    73  @[expose] def CSpec (μ : CheckMode) (env : Env) (fe : IFEnv) {α : Type}
    74      (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) : Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), CheckOK μ false env fe s₀ → P s₀.store →
    76      c s₀ = .ok (r, s') → CoreStep μ env fe s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L125-L171
   125  /-! ## The spines -/
   126  
   127  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   128  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   129  
   130  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   131  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   132  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   133  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   134  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   135      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   136      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   137        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   138    intro n
   139    induction n with
   140    | zero =>
   141      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   142      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   143      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   144      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   145    | succ n ih =>
   146      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   147      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   148      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   149      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   150      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   151      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   152      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   153      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   154      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   155          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   156            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   157        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   158        congr 1
   159        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   160        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   161        congr 1
   162        omega
   163      rw [hkey]
   164      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   165  
   166  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   167      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   168    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   169    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   170    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   171    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd
