== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L1-L30
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Refine2.Tactic.Lockstep` — the lockstep judgement and the `lockstep` tactic
     3  
     4  Task #97-T2-TACTIC.  Theorem 2 in its lockstep shape (task #97-T2-AUDIT §6)
     5  relates two programs doing the same operations in the same order, over a
     6  state relation that says only "the same data in two representations".  So a
     7  proof of one `_refines` lemma is a ZIP of two do-blocks: peel one bind on each
     8  side, close the correspondence of the two callees with a registered lemma,
     9  continue with the related results.  This file makes that zip a tactic.
    10  
    11  ## The judgement
    12  
    13  `LS pers R m lst x` — *every outcome of the Rust computation `m` is matched by
    14  the twin action `x` run from `lst`*: an `Ok a` by an `ok (b, lst')` with
    15  `R a b` in a related post-state, an `Err e` by the twin throwing at the same
    16  kind (`AErrSim`).  It is `Sim₀` with a relation for the answer instead of an
    17  abstraction function, and with the Rust equation moved into the judgement, so
    18  that the Rust program is visible in the GOAL beside the twin (`LS.toSim₀` is the
    19  bridge back).  Four companion judgements carry the other Rust callee shapes:
    20  
    21  | judgement | Rust callee shape | example |
    22  |---|---|---|
    23  | `LS`  | `Result (Result α CheckError × AState)` — state threaded | `intern_e_app`, a recursive call |
    24  | `LSR` | `Result (Result α CheckError)` — reads, may fail | `view` |
    25  | `LSV` | `Result α` — reads, total | `lift_get`, `inst_list_cutoff` |
    26  | `LSW` | `Result AState` — writes, total | `lift_set` |
    27  | `LSP` | `Result α`, **Rust only** — no twin counterpart | `fuel - 1#u64`, `dup2`, `eidx_nat_key`, `fail` |
    28  | `LSM` | `Result (Result α × AState × M)` — a memoised walk, memo beside the result | `consts_resolve_f_go`, `intern_expr_go` |
    29  | `LSRM` | `Result (Result α × M)` — a memoised reader walk | `all_level_params_defined_go` |
    30  

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L164-L168
   164  /-- **The lockstep judgement** for a state-threading Rust computation. -/
   165  def LS {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   166      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState))
   167      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   168    ∀ o st', m = ok (o, st') → LOut pers R o st' (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L170-L174
   170  /-- A Rust READ that may fail: the state is `st` before and after. -/
   171  def LSR {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   172      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError))
   173      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   174    ∀ o, m = ok o → LOut pers R o st (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L634-L646
   634  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised state walk**: `LS` of the walk with
   635  its memo moved into the answer; `R` relates `(answer, memo)` to the twin's
   636  answer (typically the twin's `(answer, memo)` pair). -/
   637  def LSM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   638      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState × M))
   639      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   640    LS pers R (packM m) lst x
   641  
   642  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised reader walk** at the state `st`. -/
   643  def LSRM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   644      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × M))
   645      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   646    LS pers R (packRM st m) lst x

  2872  /-- **The lockstep tactic**: step until every goal is closed or stuck. -/
  2873  macro "lockstep" : tactic => `(tactic| repeat' lockstep_step)

   290  theorem instantiate1_go_aux (n : Nat) :
   291      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}

   615      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L16-L135
    16  /-!
    17  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    18  
    19  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    20  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    21  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    22  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    23  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    24  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    25  
    26  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    27    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    28  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    29    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    30  
    31  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    32  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    33  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    34  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    35  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    36  
    37  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    38  
    39  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    40  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    41  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    42  
    43      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    44        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    45  
    46  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    47  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    48  of `check_main`.
    49  
    50  and the twin runs the same six stages (`Arena/Main.lean`'s
    51  `runPipelineHead`/`runPipelineTail` drive them for `con-ron-lean`).  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    52  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    53  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    54  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    55  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `h7` the freeze, `h8`
    56  phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    57  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is
    58  the contract of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's
    59  two verified closures, written out (task #98-H8): index lists `ws`, one per
    60  worker, covering every pending record, and for each a `foldlM` of
    61  `check_pending` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That
    62  contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    63  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.  `parallelAll_of_pool` reads it as
    64  `Phased.lean`'s `ParallelAll`, and `PoolAccepts.toParts` turns that into one
    65  accepting fold per worker over the records it checked.
    66  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    67  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    68  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    69  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    70  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    71  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    72  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    73  
    74  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    75     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    76     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    77     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    78  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    79     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    80     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    81     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    82     (`stages_no_False`, through the pure fold);
    83  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    84     model.
    85  
    86  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    87  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    88  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    89  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    90  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    91  
    92  ## The named hypotheses
    93  
    94  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    95  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    96  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    97  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    98  `prepare_prelude`).  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    99  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
   100  they assume is exactly:
   101  
   102  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   103    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   104    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   105    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   106    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   107    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam — the one seam left.
   108  
   109  Former hypotheses, now theorems or gone (DESIGN.md's task #97-COMPOSE and
   110  #98-HEADLINE sections tag each with its owning lane):
   111  
   112  * ~~`InitRel`~~ — the Rust start state is related to the twin's: a theorem
   113    since task #97-P5-Top (`Refine2/Checker/Init.lean`'s `init_rel`);
   114  * ~~`hk : CoreSpec .verified Arena.checkFuel`~~ — Theorem 1's Core tier
   115    spec: a theorem since task #97-P3-Core round 6
   116    (`Bridge/Checker/Hyp.lean`'s `CoreSpec.of_core`);
   117  * ~~`hind : IndSpec .verified`~~ — Theorem 1's inductive tier spec:
   118    `Bridge/Inductives/Decl.lean`'s `indSpec_of_bridge` since task #97-P3-Ind
   119    round 8 (the stage lemmas below still take it as a parameter);
   120  * ~~`hbytes`~~ — the prelude's bytes are con-leche's: not needed since task
   121    #98-HEADLINE.  con-leche's `preparePrelude` puts the prelude's records into
   122    the checked stream, so soundness holds whatever the prelude parses to
   123    (`Bridge/Frontend/Prepare.lean`'s `builtinPreludeE_run` is parametric in
   124    the bytes).  The gate `scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check` stays, as the
   125    claim that con-ron ships con-leche's prelude;
   126  * ~~`hsc : ScanSpec`~~ — Theorem 2's scanner seam: a theorem since task
   127    #97-P5-Front (`Refine2/Frontend/Scan/Spec.lean`'s `scanSpec`);
   128  * ~~`hpers`, `hest`, `hst0`~~ — the start state and tier were universally
   129    quantified with three equations; since task #98-HEADLINE they are the
   130    constants `startState`/`emptyTier` (`startState_eq`, `emptyTier_eq`);
   131  * `hdec` is now `hpins`, the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L1-L55
     1  //! `driver` — con-leche's `Driver/{Cli,CheckMain,Run}.lean`, over the ARENA (tasks #37, #48 and
     2  //! #97-P4f), and the Rust side of the Lean twin's
     3  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Main.lean`.
     4  //!
     5  //! The module is that driver in its order: the reads,
     6  //! the two phases with the boundary visible, the `--progress` heartbeat behind
     7  //! one observer trait, the verdict lines, the exit-code mapping, and the flag
     8  //! parsers.  Task #97-SWAP put it here, under the name the shipping driver
     9  //! always had: it was `crates/con-ron-arena/src/driver.rs` through the arena
    10  //! campaign, beside the `Expr`-tree driver it has now replaced, and the
    11  //! eleven representation-free items it used to import across the crate line
    12  //! ([`exit_code`], `verdict_word`, `message`, `ms_secs`, `progress_stride`,
    13  //! `jobs_count`, `default_jobs`, [`workers_for`],
    14  //! `read_up_to`, `STACK_BYTES`) are back in it, unchanged.
    15  //!
    16  //! ## THE EXIT CODES
    17  //!
    18  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |
    21  //! | 1 | `rejected` | a declaration is invalid |
    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |
    23  //! | 3 | error | bad usage, malformed input, or an internal failure of unclear cause |
    24  //!
    25  //! ## What the arena changed about the driver
    26  //!
    27  //! 1. **The state is one `AState`** (`con_ron_core::arena::monad::AState`: the
    28  //!    store, the per-call memos, the per-declaration caches), threaded as a
    29  //!    `&mut` through the parse, the preparation, the pin walk and both phases.
    30  //!    The `Expr`-tree driver threaded a `CState` and the declarations carried
    31  //!    their own terms; here the terms are in the state and the records are
    32  //!    handles into it, so nothing may be run against a state that is not the
    33  //!    one they were interned into.
    34  //! 2. **`intern_all_pins` runs once, before the fold, with the scratch tier
    35  //!    off** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d's "for P4f"): every pinned datum
    36  //!    is in the PERSISTENT cons table before any declaration's check can
    37  //!    intern one into a tier that is about to vanish.  Its result — the
    38  //!    interned pin list — is the fold's parameter.
    39  //! 3. **Phase B's bracket is `check_pending`'s**, which turns the scratch tier
    40  //!    on and drops it.  A driver that checked records itself without it would
    41  //!    grow the scratch tier without bound; the loop below calls it once per
    42  //!    record and nothing else opens a tier.
    43  //! 4. **`--jobs=<n>` runs [`crate::pool`]** (task #97-P6-6b), which is
    44  //!    DESIGN.md §8.3's arrangement and needs no atomics: the persistent tier
    45  //!    is immutable in phase B, so it is shared by reference, and each worker
    46  //!    owns a scratch tier, its own caches and a copy of the pin handles.
    47  //!    Phase B reads `fe` and the pending list and writes only the per-record
    48  //!    state, which is what lets the pool slot in where the `while` is.
    49  //!
    50  //! ## The read loop
    51  //!
    52  //! [`parse_export_handle_d`] is `ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean`'s
    53  //! `foldChunks` over forward reads (its positional reads and its parallel
    54  //! rounds parse are not ported): the VERIFIED loop `export_c::parse_source` (task
    55  //! #97-P5-Driver moved it into the core) over [`HandleSource`], the handle

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L507-L600
   507  
   508  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:317-334 checkDecls
   509  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:50-210 checkDeclsIO
   510  /// **The driver**: the two-phase fold with the boundary visible — a straight
   511  /// line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the pool for
   512  /// phase B (tasks #97-P5-Driver, #98-POOL).  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   513  ///
   514  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   515  /// |---|---|---|
   516  /// | phase A | `checker::install_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   517  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call's value |
   518  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..pend.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `check_pending tier st mode fe pend[k]` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   519  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   520  ///
   521  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   522  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   523  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every record was checked by some worker,
   524  /// each worker folding `check_pending` over the records it claimed on ONE
   525  /// `worker_state`.  Everything else here is the observer, which only ever
   526  /// holds `&` the state (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the
   527  /// other lines through `&st.store` and the worker's `&AState`), so it cannot
   528  /// change an outcome.
   529  ///
   530  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN** (task #97-P6-6b).  Phase A
   531  /// owns its persistent tier and appends to it; at the boundary
   532  /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves the four stores' persistent tables out into
   533  /// one `PersTier`, handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those
   534  /// tables, and a worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so
   535  /// every append there is a scratch append (task #98-FREEZE).  The
   536  /// installed index goes to the workers by reference, since `check_pending`
   537  /// takes the visibility bound as a scalar — so `n` workers share one
   538  /// environment and one term DAG and own nothing but a scratch tier, their
   539  /// caches and a copy of the pin handles (`checker::worker_state`).
   540  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   541      pers: &PersTier,
   542      st: &mut AState,
   543      mode: &CheckMode,
   544      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   545      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   546      jobs: u64,
   547      obs: &mut O,
   548  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   549      let total = ds.len();
   550      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   551      let p = match checker::install_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   552          Err(e) => {
   553              obs.install_failed(e.1, total);
   554              return Err(e);
   555          }
   556          Ok(p) => p,
   557      };
   558      let (_n_installed, fe, pend): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>) = p;
   559      let m = pend.len();
   560      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m);
   561      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   562      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   563      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier leaves the state and becomes a
   564      // value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   565      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   566      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   567      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store);
   568      // PHASE B: `check_pending` at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   569      // folding it over the records it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the
   570      // verdict and the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at
   571      // every `--jobs` (the least failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   572      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   573      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   574      let r = parallel_all(
   575          m,
   576          workers,
   577          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   578          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]),
   579          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, w, m, &pend[k]),
   580      );
   581      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   582          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   583          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   584      };
   585      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   586      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   587      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   588      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   589      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   590      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   591      checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   592      match phase_b_verdict(&pend, r) {
   593          Err((e, pos)) => {
   594              obs.check_failed(pos);
   595              Err((e, pos))
   596          }
   597          Ok(()) => {
   598              obs.check_done(m);
   599              Ok(fe)
   600          }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L45-L97
    45  //! ## THE TRUSTED CLAIM, and the whole of it
    46  //!
    47  //! **If `parallel_all(n, workers, init, step, after)` returns `Ok(())`, then
    48  //! every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker; each worker built its
    49  //! state with `init()` exactly once and folded `step` over the indices it
    50  //! claimed, in claim order; and every one of those `step` calls returned
    51  //! `Ok(())`** — at every worker count.  That is `ParallelAll` in
    52  //! `proof/ConRon/Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean` (task #98-POOL), and it is a
    53  //! statement about this module's control flow only — nothing about what
    54  //! `init` and `step` compute.  With the driver's closures it is the
    55  //! capstone's pool premise `h8` (task #98-H8 states it inline: index lists
    56  //! `ws` covering `0..pend.len`, and for each `w` in `ws` a `foldlM` of
    57  //! `check_pending` over `w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting), which the
    58  //! proof relates, worker by worker, to the twin (`PoolAccepts.toParts`,
    59  //! `pool_accepts_refines`).
    60  //!
    61  //! The claim is deliberately weaker than what the code does (task #98-H8):
    62  //! the counter below hands each index to exactly ONE worker and a worker's
    63  //! claims INCREASE, but the contract promises neither — the proof needs only
    64  //! coverage, since each record is checked against its own prefix environment
    65  //! and the twin's grouping theorem (`checkPendingList_grouping`) holds for any
    66  //! order, any split and any repetition.  The argument:
    67  //!
    68  //! * **A claim is a `fetch_add` on one counter.**  Each value `0, 1, 2, …` is
    69  //!   handed to exactly one caller, so every index in `0..n` is claimed (by
    70  //!   exactly one worker, in fact).  A worker stops at its first claim `≥ n`.
    71  //! * **A worker is one fold.**  `worker` calls `init()` once, then for each
    72  //!   claimed index `k` calls `step(&mut st, k)` on that one state — the fold,
    73  //!   in claim order.  `after(&st, k)` sees the state by `&` only.  A claimed
    74  //!   index at or above `limit` is skipped without a call, and on an accepting
    75  //!   run the limit never moves (only a failing step lowers it), so no claimed
    76  //!   index is skipped.
    77  //! * **Merge by index — master's argument.**  A worker hands back each index
    78  //!   it stepped with the step's result; the workers' arrays are merged *by
    79  //!   index* into one table and `first_failure` walks it in index order,
    80  //!   answering `Ok` only if every slot holds `Ok`.  So an accept means every
    81  //!   index was stepped, successfully, by the worker that claimed it, whatever
    82  //!   the timing.  An empty slot is `ParallelError::Missing`, never `Ok`.
    83  //!
    84  //! The failure side is not part of the claim the capstone uses, but the pool
    85  //! keeps master's behaviour there: the walk stops at the first failing index,
    86  //! and the table is complete below it.  con-leche's argument: a worker whose
    87  //! step fails at `f` lowers the shared `limit` to `f`, and a worker skips a
    88  //! claimed index at or above the limit.  Every value the limit ever holds is
    89  //! `n` or a *failing* index, hence at least the first failing index `f`; so an
    90  //! index below `f` is never skipped, and — the counter being monotone — it was
    91  //! claimed before `f` was and is finished by the worker that claimed it.
    92  //! `pool_reports_the_first_failure_at_every_jobs` is the test, at 1, 2, 3, 4
    93  //! and 8 workers on a list whose records 2 and 4 both fail;
    94  //! `pool_is_the_one_worker_walk_at_every_jobs` checks that phase B's verdict
    95  //! is the one-worker walk's; `parallel_all_partitions_the_indices` checks the
    96  //! claim itself on a state that records its claims.
    97  //!

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean#L328-L332
   328  def ParallelAll {S E : Type} (n : Nat) (init : Result S)
   329      (step : S → Nat → Result (core.result.Result Unit E × S)) : Prop :=
   330    ∃ parts : List (List Nat),
   331      (∀ k < n, ∃ w ∈ parts, k ∈ w) ∧
   332      ∀ w ∈ parts, ∃ s₀, init = ok s₀ ∧ FoldAllOk step s₀ w

== scripts/gates.sh#L6-L36
     6  # Runs, in order, and stops at the first failure:
     7  #   1. cargo build                          the crate compiles, warning-free
     8  #   2. cargo test                           the unit tests pass
     9  #   3. scripts/lint-rust-style.sh           the Aeneas subset (§3.4), both crates
    10  #      scripts/dead-rust.py --check         no `pub` Rust item without a caller
    11  #                                           (task #105)
    12  #   4. scripts/provenance.py check          every item cites con-leche (§3.7)
    13  #      scripts/pin-last.py                  no commit but the tip moves the
    14  #                                           con-leche pin (§7, task #108)
    15  #   5. scripts/provenance-selftest.py        the gate's Lean parser and the
    16  #                                           bump classifier, on their fixtures
    17  #   6. scripts/twin-lines.py check          every `Lean twin:` line names a
    18  #                                           declaration of `proof/ConRon/**` at
    19  #                                           its current lines (§3.7)
    20  #   7. scripts/overview-links.sh            OVERVIEW.md/DESIGN.md line anchors
    21  #   8. scripts/holes.sh --check             OVERVIEW.md §8.1 == the model's holes
    22  #   9. scripts/gen-pins.sh --check          embedded pin text == natOpPinSets
    23  #  10. scripts/gen-prelude.sh --check       embedded prelude text == con-leche's
    24  #  11. scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check  (B)'s embedded prelude bytes, ditto
    25  #  12. scripts/extract.sh --check           committed generated Lean == crate
    26  #  13. cd proof && lake build               the default targets elaborate: every
    27  #                                           library of the chain, Theorem 1
    28  #                                           (`ConRonBridge`), Theorem 2
    29  #                                           (`ConRonRefine2`), the composition
    30  #                                           (`ConRonCapstone`) included; any
    31  #      warning from proof/'s own sources fails it (lake-build-wfail.sh, #102)
    32  #      (LAKE_JOBS=N caps lake's parallelism through LEAN_NUM_THREADS — Lake 5
    33  #      has no jobs flag; the first con-leche build can exhaust memory, #74)
    34  #  14. scripts/dead-census-gate.sh          no declaration of proof/ConRon/**
    35  #                                           unreachable from the headline
    36  #                                           theorems, Tests and tooling (#105)
